3ff244a19b79: Write three sentences: «Mam wózek», «Nie mam wózka», «Szukam wózka». Ask the student to spot the difference before you explain anything.
c3ffea06b7db: The same logic as in the locative from lesson 5. Remind them in one sentence.
ce1dd6b4296f: There is no reliable rule for things. Say so directly: living beings — always -a, the rest we learn together with the word.
c16c3f442305: The easiest theory slide. Go through it quickly — it is a gift after the previous one.
ca61353945bd: Ask the student to add an adjective to the three forms from the previous slides — this tests both rules together.
1832544d3d0b: The second and third forms look «cut short» — this surprises learners most. Have them say it aloud.
48612b9d2052: This is the main rule of the lesson. Give five pairs of sentences for speed before moving on.
40012a211c21: Cover the right-hand column and ask the student to form the ending on their own. The last row is the hardest.
2f19a1ed704d: Read all six, then close the slide and ask the student to name the prepositions from memory.
a76f88ba8a75: English has no cases: «I'm looking for a job». This is where the mistake «szukam pracę» is born.
2aa9e999de09: The first trap is a construction, the second and third are verb government (which case a verb takes). Read the English version word for word, otherwise the mistake is not visible.
62afc1926486: The last trap is phonetic, not grammatical. Ask them to say both versions out loud and hear that the first one cannot be pronounced.
